cypher: MATCH (g:gene {name: "PTPN22"}) WITH collect(DISTINCT g) AS nodes, [] AS edges RETURN nodes, edges;
summary:
PTPN22, a protein-coding gene located on chromosome 1, encodes the lymphoid tyrosine phosphatase involved in immune system regulation. It plays a critical role in T1D susceptibility and immune modulation. Genetic studies have identified PTPN22 as a major non-HLA risk factor for T1D, with the R620W variant being strongly associated with increased disease risk and altered immune signaling. This variant affects T-cell receptor signaling, antigen presentation, and cytokine production, contributing to autoimmunity [pubmed id: 23193190, 28751955, 30139951, 24364806]. Functional studies in mice have demonstrated that PTPN22 variation impacts the B-cell compartment and provides protection against autoimmune diabetes when knocked down [pubmed id: 31732921].

Mechanistically, PTPN22 participates in immune-related pathways, such as T-cell activation and immune response regulation, and interacts with proteins like VIM, CRK, and EGFR, which are involved in cytoskeletal organization, signal transduction, and cell proliferation, respectively. It also regulates other genes, such as RPS19BP1, VAV1, and MIB1, further highlighting its integral role in immune signaling networks. These insights make PTPN22 a potential therapeutic target in managing autoimmune diabetes.
